items.claim: On Oct 19, 2026, GitHub deprecated GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3.7 Flash and Grok 4.5 across most Copilot experiences. Suggested replacements include GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Grok 4.7.
items.why_it_matters: Workflows pinned to these models need a supported replacement, and enterprise admins may need to enable the replacements in their model policy.
items.try_this: Search your Copilot settings and scripts for the deprecated model names and switch each one to the alternative GitHub suggests.

verification.method: Model table read on GitHub's own changelog entry

items.excerpt: Copilot Enterprise administrators may need to enable access to alternative models through their model policies in Copilot settings.

items.claim: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT-licensed weights and a 1M-token context. The API costs $0.30 input and $1.20 output per million tokens at peak, half that off-peak. The deepseek-v4-flash name now routes to it.
items.why_it_matters: If you use the legacy name, your app is already on a new model. The open weights are also a cheap long-context option.
items.try_this: If your code calls deepseek-v4-flash, rerun your evals now, because that name is now served by V4.1-Flash-1017.

verification.method: Price, context and routing checked on DeepSeek's pricing and news pages; MIT license on the HF model card. Parameter counts did not match, so they are omitted

items.claim: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash on Oct 19, 2026. API prices are $0.15 input, $0.60 output and $0.015 cached input per million tokens. MiniMax says weights come later and gives no date.
items.why_it_matters: It is a low-cost agentic model. Latent Space reported an Oct 23 weights date that MiniMax's own page does not confirm.
items.try_this: Test it through the MiniMax API on your own agent tasks, and don't plan self-hosting until MiniMax publishes a weights date.

verification.method: Release date and pricing checked on MiniMax blog; benchmark scores left out as vendor claims

items.claim: Inception released Mercury 3, a diffusion LLM with a 1M-token context. It is available through Inception's OpenAI-compatible API, OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel.
items.why_it_matters: Diffusion models generate text differently from token-by-token models. With an OpenAI-compatible API, you can try one with almost no code changes.
items.try_this: Point an existing OpenAI-compatible client at Inception's API for one latency-sensitive task and compare quality and speed with your current model.

verification.method: Launch post read on Inception's blog; speed and benchmark comparisons left out as vendor claims

items.claim: Claude Code v2.1.304 fixes a bug where claude --worktree removed the worktree and its branch at exit without asking, when HEAD was detached or on another branch. That could lose commits.
items.why_it_matters: If you run agents in worktrees, older versions could silently delete branches that hold unmerged work.
items.try_this: Run claude update, then check that claude --version reports 2.1.304 or later before using --worktree on a detached HEAD.

verification.method: Line confirmed in the official GitHub release notes; no sandbox run
verification.audit_note: v2.1.304 release notes confirm the --worktree fix: it removed the worktree and branch without asking when HEAD was detached or elsewhere, risking lost commits.

items.excerpt: Fixed claude --worktree removing the worktree and its branch without asking at exit

items.claim: In Claude Code v2.1.304, setting CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200k no longer silently gives a 100K window. The variable now accepts k and M suffixes and warns when a value is out of range or ignored.
items.why_it_matters: Anyone who set this variable with a suffix may have been compacting at half the window they intended.
items.try_this: If you set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, update and watch the startup output for a warning about an ignored or out-of-range value.

verification.method: Line confirmed in the official GitHub release notes; no sandbox run

items.excerpt: the variable now accepts k and M suffixes like --autocompact

items.claim: vLLM v0.32.0 is out with 814 commits. It adds an NVFP4 KV cache on SM8x, SM12x and SM90 GPUs, a 4-bit KV cache on ROCm, a GPU n-gram speculator in Model Runner V2, and least-loaded routing across API servers.
items.why_it_matters: Lower-precision KV cache and better multi-server routing can raise throughput on self-hosted serving without new hardware.
items.try_this: Before upgrading, read the v0.32.0 notes on --api-server-count routing and KV cache dtypes, then benchmark on your own traffic.

verification.method: Features checked in the official GitHub release notes; throughput gains are the PR's own benchmark

items.claim: Claude Code v2.1.304 adds /claude-api managed-agents-secure. It compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide and reports differences without changing anything.
items.why_it_matters: It gives you a read-only security check for hosted agents before you deploy them.
items.try_this: Run /claude-api managed-agents-secure on one existing Managed Agents agent and review the gaps it lists against the security guide.

verification.method: Command listed in the official GitHub release notes; not run

items.excerpt: compares a Managed Agents agent's settings with Anthropic's published security guide, without changing anything

items.claim: GitHub made REST GET and PATCH endpoints for Copilot model policies generally available. They work at the enterprise, enterprise team, enterprise app and organization levels, for example /orgs/{org}/copilot/model-policies.
items.why_it_matters: Admins can now script which models are allowed across orgs instead of clicking through settings.
items.try_this: As an org admin, call GET /orgs/{org}/copilot/model-policies to audit which models are enabled before you PATCH anything.

verification.method: Endpoints listed on GitHub's changelog; the REST docs page for these endpoints was not found at the guessed URL

items.excerpt: GET and PATCH endpoints are now generally available for model policies at four levels

items.claim: Google Research open-sourced Harness² (google-research/harness2, Apache 2.0). It lets an agent rewrite its own harness, including prompts, memory, skills, scripts and plugins, while model weights stay frozen.
items.why_it_matters: It treats harness tuning as automatable, which is the layer most builders tune by hand today.
items.try_this: Read the repo README's list of eight editable harness components and compare it with what you currently tune by hand in your agent.

verification.method: Repo, license and design checked in the README; reported gains differ from Latent Space's figures; not run

items.claim: OpenAI published a post on improving ChatGPT coding in low-resource programming languages. It introduces new evaluations for software engineering, SQLite and COBOL migration.
items.why_it_matters: Teams maintaining legacy COBOL or niche-language code may get better model support and new benchmarks to judge it.

verification.method: Article returned 403; post existence and eval list confirmed in OpenAI's own RSS feed; improvement claims not checked

items.excerpt: with new evaluations for software engineering, SQLite, and COBOL migration
